name: Taunton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Taunton, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Taunton, MA, the Christmas City: the Lights On Festival, Santa's house on the Taunton Green and the Christmas Parade.
lede: Taunton calls itself the Christmas City, and it earns the name: the whole downtown turns into a festival when the Taunton Green lights up, Santa moves into a little house on the Green for December, and a parade rolls down Broadway the next day.
celebrates: Everything in Taunton centers on the Taunton Green. The City of Taunton's Lighting of the Green and Lights On Festival fills downtown with more than 30 entertainment sites on one Saturday in early December, from a free Christmas Kids Fair and trackless train rides to a petting zoo, hayrides and a laser light show, and Santa arrives as the lights switch on. After the festival, Santa stays in his house on the Green on weekend evenings, Victorian Carolers stroll on Friday and Saturday nights, and the light display and music stay up through New Year's Day. The city's Christmas Parade follows the festival, starting on Broadway and ending at City Hall.
lastyear: In 2025 the city held its Lights On Festival on Saturday, December 6, from 3 to 8 pm, under the theme Once Upon a Christmas in the Silver City, with a reading of The Night Before Christmas. The Taunton Christmas Parade followed on Sunday, December 7. The Taunton Daily Gazette's 2025 list also had a live reading of A Christmas Carol at the Old Colony History Museum on Church Green.
facts: Taunton was settled by members of the Plymouth Colony and incorporated as a town in 1639, making it one of the oldest towns in the United States. It became a city in 1864. In the 1800s it earned the nickname Silver City because silver makers such as Reed and Barton and F. B. Rogers worked there. Since December 1914 the city has lit up the Taunton Green each December, which gave Taunton its second nickname, the Christmas City.
trains: Since March 2025, the MBTA Fall River/New Bedford Line has served East Taunton station, where the Fall River and New Bedford branches meet, with trains to and from Boston's South Station. That makes a train trip to the Christmas City possible from Boston. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs its Christmas train through the lights. The Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River sits farther down the same new rail line.

kidfact: Taunton has turned on Christmas lights on its town green every December since 1914. That is more than 110 years of lights, which is why people call Taunton the Christmas City.
faq: Why is Taunton called the Christmas City?

Taunton has put up a large holiday light display on the Taunton Green every December since 1914. The yearly Lighting of the Green grew into the Lights On Festival, which fills downtown with entertainment on one Saturday in early December, and the display stays up through New Year's Day. That long tradition gave the city its nickname.
How much does the Taunton Lights On Festival cost?

The festival sells admission buttons for adults and teens, and children 12 and under get in free. Buttons are sold ahead at City Hall, the Parks and Recreation office and several downtown businesses while supplies last, and also on the day at Santa's Village on the Green and other spots downtown.
When can kids see Santa in Taunton?

Santa arrives on the Taunton Green when the lights switch on at the Lights On Festival, and he also visits families at Bristol County Savings Bank that night. After the festival he stays in his house on the Green on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings from 5 to 8 pm in December, and pictures are complimentary.
Is there a Christmas parade in Taunton?

Yes. The City of Taunton holds its Christmas Parade the day after the Lights On Festival. It starts on Broadway at noon and ends at City Hall. City Hall also hosts raffle tables during the Lights On Festival to help support the parade, along with photos with Mrs. Claus and Mad Science shows.
Can we take the train to Taunton?

Yes. The MBTA Fall River/New Bedford Line stops at East Taunton station, with trains to and from Boston's South Station. On festival day, downtown roads close at 2 pm, and families driving in can park at Bristol Community College on Hamilton Street and ride the free GATRA shuttle to the Green.
